patterns.name: Side Volley
patterns.notes: Alternating side volleys. Each is a wall of projectiles with two openings, so the player must read the gap and move to it rather than stand still.

patterns.name: Diagonal Whip
patterns.notes: A thin chain whips corner to corner: the line is the danger, so the dodge is standing off it, not leaving a band. Two diagonals per bar so the second is read from the first.

patterns.name: Safe Ground
patterns.notes: The floor arms and one patch stays safe. The telegraph draws the refuge positively, so the read is "get to the green square", not "leave the red one" -- the two halves of the same lesson AP01 teaches.

patterns.name: Chain Corridor
patterns.notes: Two parallel chains wall off a safe channel that slides across the arena between bars. The channel is floored by the fairness minimum, so it is always wide enough to stand in -- the play is reaching it in time.

patterns.name: Serpent Chain
patterns.notes: A snake of chain with a slowly drifting midline, then a zig-zag that cuts across it. The sine drift is small enough to follow at a walk.

patterns.name: Spiral Out
patterns.notes: A spiral of projectiles unwinds from the centre. The arm rotates as it fires, so the player is walking against a curve rather than sidestepping a line.

patterns.name: Rhythm Window
patterns.notes: The sweep window stops being static: its centre steps once per beat along gapPath, so the wall has a choreography and the player reads the next position on the pulse.

patterns.name: Spray And Pendulum
patterns.notes: A rotating spray walks its bursts around the arena while a pendulum arm swings back across the path. Both threats advertise their direction before they move.

patterns.name: Spray Rotation
patterns.notes: One spray, one direction, one step per beat: the first two bursts are the lesson and the rest are the test. Swap CW for CCW on the repeat so the read is not memorised.

patterns.name: Alternating Spray
patterns.notes: ALTERNATE spray: the stream walks out and then back, so the gap the player used is the gap that closes next. Two arms with a pendulum fan underneath.

patterns.name: Ring Collapse
patterns.notes: The ring collapses onto the player and then blows back out. The window rotates between the two, so the safe spot is a place, not a memorised angle.

patterns.name: Spray Double Time
patterns.notes: Eighth-note emissions: three blades per bar. The rotation is still one direction, so the read is the same -- only the tempo of the read changes.

patterns.name: Safe Tile Sweep
patterns.notes: Safe tiles carve the floor into islands while a straight wall sweeps across. The wall has one static window, so the tile the player commits to has to be on the window line.

patterns.name: Fan And Spray
patterns.notes: Three fan arms sweeping one way and a spray walking the other. The two rotations are deliberately out of phase: there is a safe wedge, but it moves.

patterns.name: Pendulum Fan
patterns.notes: The fan reverses on a fixed cycle, so its arc is a metronome the player can stand still beside -- as long as they stand on the right side of the turning point.

patterns.name: Spiral Inward
patterns.notes: The same spiral, fired inward and turning the other way. The window is a moving notch on the rim, so the player tracks the rotation rather than a fixed angle.

patterns.name: Shrinking Window
patterns.notes: The sweep window tightens as the wall crosses, so a late entry is a narrower entry. The floor is the fairness minimum: it never closes past what the player fits through.

patterns.name: Laser And Ring Climax
patterns.notes: A rotating spray walks the arena while two lasers close across it, and the bar ends with the ring collapsing onto whatever the player committed to. Every threat advertises itself; the difficulty is that they advertise at once.

patterns.name: Sector Chase
patterns.notes: Wedges of the arena go off in turn, first clockwise in sixths and then anticlockwise in quarters. There is no gap to find -- the whole answer is walking the rim at the sweep's pace, and the reversal is the part that punishes memorising one direction.

patterns.name: Sector And Spray
patterns.notes: The sweep skips every other wedge, so the player is moving twice as far per step, and a rotating spray lays fire across the arena while they do it. The closing ring is the only thing here that asks for a *place* rather than a pace.

patterns.name: Shifting Ground
patterns.notes: The refuge drifts instead of sitting still, and it relocates on the bar: around the circle for two bars -- starting opposite each time, so the drift cannot be camped -- then side to side for two. Standing in the right place is not enough any more; the player has to keep arriving.

patterns.name: Quadrant Rotation
patterns.notes: Only a quarter of the arena is ever safe, and which quarter rotates on the bar. Coarse and rhythmic: the crossing is made on the pulse, not steered, which is the point -- it is the one safe-zone form that is a movement *timing* problem rather than a positioning one.

patterns.name: Chain Formation
patterns.notes: The same squad of chains, re-formed every bar: abreast, fanned out, sweeping on a pivot, then arced. The ask never changes -- find the lane that is not a chain -- so each bar is a fresh read of one familiar verb rather than a new threat.

patterns.name: Floor Stripes
patterns.notes: Where is safe, drawn in bigger and bigger strokes: one row, one column, both at once, then a quarter wedge. The warning length is the escape walk, so the cross telegraphs longer than the strip -- the shapes teach themselves.

patterns.name: Double Jump
patterns.notes: Two jumps back to back, rest, one more. The first taste of a chain.

patterns.name: Triple Chain
patterns.notes: A jump on every beat for a full bar.

patterns.name: Short Gap Chain
patterns.notes: Gap, spike, gap, slide. Mixes the three obstacle answers in one phrase.

patterns.name: Bounce Chain
patterns.notes: Pad launches into a spike clear; the bar ends on a quick double.

patterns.name: Half Beat Jumps
patterns.notes: Syncopated eighths. The jump becomes a way of playing the percussion line.

patterns.name: Rapid Stair
patterns.notes: Rising spikes then a slide, so the phrase resolves downward.

patterns.name: Gravity Entry
patterns.notes: Flip on the downbeat, then keep running on the ceiling without a pause.

patterns.name: Gravity Alternation
patterns.notes: Flip, three jumps along the ceiling, flip again, and land back on the floor for the closing pair. Obstacles are tagged to the surface the player is actually on.

patterns.name: Runner Climax
patterns.notes: Everything at once at eighth-note density. The pattern the whole mode builds toward.

patterns.name: Ceiling Chain
patterns.notes: The full inversion sentence: flip up, jump-slide-jump-jump along the ceiling, gravity restores itself and the phrase resolves with two floor jumps.

patterns.name: Mixed Chain
patterns.notes: Every obstacle type in one phrase, one answer per half bar: jump, pad, jump, slide, gap, jump, jump, slide. Each landing sets up the next input.

patterns.name: Recovery
patterns.notes: Two jumps in four bars. Deliberately almost empty -- somewhere to put the player down after a climax so the next one lands.

patterns.name: Sustain
patterns.notes: Two long holds. Teaches press, keep holding, release.

patterns.name: Taps Into Hold
patterns.notes: A rising three-tap phrase that resolves into a sustain -- the shape of a sung line.

patterns.name: Drift Up
patterns.notes: One long note sliding lane 1 -> 4 over six beats. The first drift hold a player meets.

patterns.name: Drift Zigzag
patterns.notes: A drift that descends and comes back -- tracing a melody rather than a ramp.

patterns.name: Hold Plus Taps
patterns.notes: Left hand sustains while the right hand plays the accents.

patterns.name: Vertical Climax
patterns.notes: Chords, a run, then a descending drift with accents over the top.

patterns.name: Diagonal Cycle
patterns.notes: The four diagonals on their own, so two-key entry gets learned before it is mixed in.

patterns.name: Clockwise 8
patterns.notes: A full eight-step turn clockwise, one step per beat across two bars.

patterns.name: Counterclockwise 8
patterns.notes: The same turn reversed. Good A/B for whether the rotation direction reads.

patterns.name: Cardinal Diagonal Alternation
patterns.notes: Alternating one-key and two-key entries -- the hardest thing about eight directions.

patterns.name: Diagonal Opposite Pairs
patterns.notes: Both diagonal axes, one per half bar.

patterns.name: Spiral 8
patterns.notes: Cardinals first then diagonals, on eighths. Dense but the shape is a simple rule.

patterns.name: Star
patterns.notes: Skipping three steps each time draws a star. Feels unpredictable, is completely regular.

patterns.name: Radial Climax
patterns.notes: Four opposite pairs, then a full clockwise turn at double speed.

patterns.name: Platform Step
patterns.notes: Two low platforms: at 0.04 high the runner walks up without jumping, so the lesson is that a platform is terrain before it is an obstacle.

patterns.name: Platform Hop
patterns.notes: A single jump-height platform per bar. The front face is the obstacle and the top is the reward: land on it and the beat after is free.

patterns.name: Staircase Up
patterns.notes: Three risers on consecutive beats, each one higher than the last. Every step is a jump, and the landing of one is the take-off of the next.

patterns.name: Platform Ladder
patterns.notes: Platforms on the half-beat, alternating a low step and a full hop, with a spike on the ground at the end of the bar so the ground route is never the answer.

patterns.name: Gap Bridge
patterns.notes: A gap with a platform parked over its far side. The jump clears the gap, the platform is what the player lands on -- one obstacle doing two jobs.

patterns.name: Platform Leap
patterns.notes: A gap whose only landing is a high platform over the middle. The take-off is fixed by the gap edge, so the jump is committed to before the platform is under the player.

patterns.name: Gravity Shelf
patterns.notes: The flip arrives and the shelf is already on the ceiling: the player lands on the new surface a step above it, and the second shelf is a real jump.

patterns.name: Gravity Corridor
patterns.notes: Two flips, shelves on both surfaces, and a spike after the first flip so the ceiling is not optional. The read is which surface the next shelf belongs to.

patterns.name: Platform Climax
patterns.notes: The full vocabulary at once: a bridge, a ladder on the half-beat, a flip with a shelf already waiting, and a low wall closing the bar. No bar repeats the one before it.

patterns.name: Platform Recovery
patterns.notes: One low shelf per bar and nothing else: a landing beat the player can breathe on without the runner ever stopping.
